data.name: Athalia
data.gender_notes: Athalia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'Athena', meaning 'goddess'. Athalia is a powerful and nurturing name, symbolizing strength, wisdom, and protection. In the Old Testament, Athalia is the name of a queen who tries to usurp the throne from her young nephew. The name Athalia carries the meaning “Goddess of the earth, mother” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Athalia usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the earth, mother and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name filled with the divine feminine energy of creation and nurturing.
data.etymology: Athalia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the earth, mother.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Athalia total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Athalia is of rich and diverse origins. Derived from the Greek 'Athena', it carries the cultural weight of ancient goddess worship from the classical world. In the English literary tradition, Athalia is most famously presented in the play "The Queen-Mother" by John Webster. This tragic drama portrays an evil queen who seeks to usurp the throne and destroy her nephew, King Epicurean. This representation adds a darker layer to the name, with Athalia symbolizing both strength and destruction.
data.spiritual_significance: Athalia embodies the complex nature of strength- both its protective and destructive aspects. In various religious contexts, Athalia represents the warrior goddess who shields and supports her people, yet also bears the potential to wield her power for destruction. From a spiritual perspective, the name calls for the recognition of the inherent power within each of us, encouraging the balance between using our strength for growth and healing, and avoiding the destructive potential that comes from its misuse.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Athalia represents the arrogant and destructive power of human ambition. In the biblical story of her reign, she usurped the throne from her young nephew, sacrificing innocence and love for her own desires. This symbolizes the corrupting influence of pride and the tragic consequences of misusing power.

biblical_reference.note: Reference to Athaliah, a queen of Judah in 2 Kings 8:25-26, known for her cruelty and ruthlessness

historical_references.reference: Athalia was a queen of Judah in the Old Testament who reigned in place of her son, Solomon, whom she had murdered.
historical_references.context: The story of Athalia is told in the Books of Kings (1 Kings 1:17-27) and Chronicles (2 Chronicles 13:1-12) in the Old Testament.

historical_references.reference: Athalia, also known as Matilda, was a German princess who attempted to usurp the English throne in the late 12th century during the Anarchy.
historical_references.context: The story of Athalia (Matilda) is often told in connection with the power struggle between Empress Matilda (daughter of Henry I of England) and Stephen of Blois, which followed the death of Henry I in 1135 CE. Matilda's claim to the throne was based on her being the eldest living descendant of King Henry I, but she was ultimately unsuccessful.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Athalia is of biblical origin and is most notably associated with a queen in the Old Testament book of Kings who persecutes her own son. Today, this name is seen in various modern contexts, particularly in the realms of fantasy literature, musical theater, and other artistic mediums. In fantasy literature, Athalia can be found in novels such as 'The Queen's Thief' series by Megan Whalen Turner, where she is a powerful and cunning sorceress, and in the 'Fables' comic book series by Bill Willingham. In musical theater, Athalia is the title character of a tragic opera composed by Georg Friedrich Händel in the early 18th century, and her story has been adapted into various productions and performances around the world. The name Athalia also appears in modern popular culture, such as in the video game 'The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim,' where a character named Queen Athalia is a powerful sorceress and the leader of a secretive coven.
